definition: The feast of St Martin, kept on November 11; traditionally a British and European term-day marking the turn toward winter.
etymology: It began as Old English Martinmæsse, literally “St Martin’s mass.” The name honors Martin of Tours, the fourth-century soldier-saint famed for sharing his cloak with a beggar.
usage: By Martinmas, the last leaves had loosened from the ash and the fields looked ready for winter.
